newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hutchison hopes for Oriental Plaza approval soon.
newsitem.headline: Hutchison hopes for Oriental Plaza approval soon.

text.p: Hutchison Whampoa Ltd chairman Li Ka-shing said on Thursday he hoped Chinese authorities would approve the construction of the company's Oriental Plaza property development in Beijing by July.
Hutchison Whampoa and Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd together hold a controlling stake in the project.

"We heard the project has been approved but we have not got the document yet and we hope we will get the document soon and construction could start before July 1," Li told reporters after Hutchison's annual general meeting.
He said the total investment for the project was estimated at US$2 billion, higher than original estimates. He did not elaborate on the original estimate.
He said HK$2 billion had already been invested. The design had changed from the original layout with the total floor area lower than the six million square feet initially planned.
The development of office, hotel, residential and retail space will also include an exhibition hall to house archaelogical findings at the site, Li said.
Besides Hutchison and Cheung Kong, shareholders include Orient Overseas (International) Ltd and the People's Insurance Co of China.
